newsitem.title: UK: OPEC governors to meet Oct 29 to decide on budget.
newsitem.headline: OPEC governors to meet Oct 29 to decide on budget.

text.p: OPEC's board of governors will meet on October 29 in Vienna to finalise the oil producers' group operating budget for next year and look at the progress of its restructuring programme, OPEC sources said on Wednesday.

The board, representing all 11 OPEC member states, will also set the agenda for OPEC's next ministerial conference in November where it will decide on production levels for at least the first half of 1997.
"We have to decide on the new budget and look at the phasing in of the restructuring plans," one OPEC official said.
After eliminating about 20-25 jobs at the Vienna Secretariat since the start of the year because of budget shortfalls, OPEC is not expected to make any further job cuts next year, the sources said.
"Hopefully, we have done all we need to do at this stage," one official said.
OPEC was forced to slim down operations at its headquarters after several members failed to pay their annual membership fees of nearly $2 million each.
The fees, which are equal for all OPEC members regardless of size, have been a bone of contention for the group's smaller members who say the system is unfair.

Gabon's resignation from the group was accepted at the last OPEC ministerial conference in June after Libreville's request for a lower membership fee was denied. Ecuador quit OPEC in 1992, and it also cited the high membership fee as one reason.
Iraq, forbidden since 1990 from selling its oil on world markets, has not paid any fees to OPEC in six years.
"When you have three members of 13 not paying dues, it naturally creates some big holes," one OPEC official said.

Influential OPEC members like Saudi Arabia and Iran are against changing the membership fee structure since the flat fee system theoretically insures that all OPEC members have an equal say in decision-making.
"The same fee for all system is there for a reason. Could you imagine what would happen if one member is seen paying more than the others?" one OPEC delegate said.
